_note: TARGET-FILE CORRECTION: partition_hfs_file_system_reader.cpp (484 lines) is a thin dispatcher/exporter; ALL of the untrusted HFS+ decode the brief names (catalog B-tree, extents/overflow, decmpfs, fork-size, volume geometry) lives in the header it includes, include/sak/partition_hfs_internal.h (the HfsReader engine, 12069 lines -- this is the 'large file with similar lines'). The harness snapshots/greps/mutates each mutant's own "file" and rebuilds the target, which recompiles partition_hfs_file_system_reader.cpp AND partition_hfs_file_system_writer.cpp (both #include this header), so header mutations take effect. Every find below was verified grep -Fc == 1 in the header.

mutants.why: volumeExceedsDeviceLength() must reject only volumes whose end runs PAST the device; a volume that exactly fills the device (volumeEnd == deviceLength) is legal. Relaxing > to >= rejects the exact-fit volume. hfsFileSystemReader_rejectsVolumeGeometryPastDeviceEnd loads the exact-fit 64-block-in-64-block fixture and asserts QVERIFY2(ok.ok, ...) (listDirectory on the exact fixture).

volumeExceedsEmbeddedExtent() bounds a WRAPPED (HFS-inside-HFS-wrapper) volume by its embedded extent, not the whole device; a volume exactly filling the extent is legal. Relaxing > to >= rejects the exact-fit wrapped volume. hfsFileSystemReader_rejectsWrappedVolumePastEmbeddedExtent loads the exact-fit 64-blocks-in-64-block-extent fixture and asserts it still loads (QVERIFY2(ok.ok) after the over-claim rejection block).

tryReadCompressedFile() must route an inline decmpfs type (3/7) to decodeCompressedInlineFile; misrouting the branch to the resource predicate sends inline types to 'not supported' and resource types (4/8) into the inline decoder. hfsFileSystemReader_readsDecmpfsCompressedFiles asserts the type-4 resource read QVERIFY2(resourceRead.ok) and QCOMPARE(resourceRead.data, resourceContent), plus the type-3 inline round-trip via verifyHfsCompressedReadBack -- both break.

findChild()'s case-insensitive fallback (reached only on a non-binary HFS+ volume) resolves a mixed-case path component against the on-disk name. Forcing a case-sensitive compare makes the HFS+ case-insensitive lookup fail. hfsFileSystemReader_listsDirectoriesAndReadsFiles lists the lowercase path "/docs" and asserts QVERIFY2(docs.ok, ...) and QCOMPARE(docs.entries.size(), 1) for the on-disk "Docs" folder.

recordOffsets() fail-closes on any B-tree record offset below the node descriptor or past the node end; changing || to && makes the two bounds mutually exclusive so no offset is ever rejected (fail-open). hfsFileSystemReader_checksCatalogConsistency corrupts a leaf record offset to 1 and asserts QVERIFY(!blocked.ok) and blockers contain "record offset"; with the guard weakened neither holds.

appendExtentsOverflowRecords() must keep parsed overflow-extent records that carry extents; inverting the emptiness test drops every real overflow record and keeps only empty ones, so the catalog/file forks that need overflow extents can no longer be read. hfsFileSystemReader_usesOverflowExtentsForCatalogAndFiles asserts QVERIFY2(root.ok, ...) and QCOMPARE(hello.data, expectedHello) (ending in the overflow tail), both of which require the overflow extents.

A catalog file's reported byte size is the fork logical_size, not its allocation-block count; substituting total_blocks reports blocks-as-bytes. hfsFileSystemReader_usesOverflowExtentsForCatalogAndFiles asserts QCOMPARE(root.entries.first().size_bytes, static_cast<uint64_t>(expectedHello.size())), which fails once size_bytes carries the block count instead of the byte length.

A file's resource-fork byte size is the fork logical_size, not its block count; substituting total_blocks reports blocks-as-bytes. hfsFileSystemReader_usesOverflowExtentsForCatalogAndFiles asserts QCOMPARE(root.entries.first().resource_fork_size_bytes, static_cast<uint64_t>(expectedResource.size())), which fails once resource_fork_size_bytes carries the block count instead of the byte length.
